name: Frontend developer
summary: Build fast, accessible interfaces with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React.
outcome: Ship responsive, accessible web apps from a Figma design and deploy them.

stages.title: Web basics
stages.goal: Make pages that look right on every screen.
stages.build: Three Frontend Mentor pages matched closely on mobile and desktop, deployed with live links.
stages.prove: Live links in your README plus a Lighthouse accessibility score above 90.

stages.title: JavaScript for real
stages.goal: Understand the language, not just copy it.
stages.build: A to-do or expense app with local storage, filtering and keyboard support, without a framework.
stages.prove: A clean Git history with small, well-named commits.

stages.title: React and TypeScript
stages.goal: Build component-based apps with typed data.
stages.build: A real app that calls a public API, with loading, empty and error states and routing.
stages.prove: Deployed on Vercel with a short write-up of decisions you made.

stages.title: Production skills
stages.goal: Work like a professional frontend engineer.
stages.build: A Next.js app with auth, a database and tests, plus a performance pass with before and after numbers.
stages.prove: Two portfolio projects, an open source pull request and a blog post on one hard bug.

name: Backend developer
summary: Design APIs, model data and run services that stay up.
outcome: Build and deploy a tested REST API with a database, auth, caching and CI.

stages.title: Language and tools
stages.goal: Get fluent in one backend language and your terminal.
stages.build: Three small CLI tools in your chosen language, each with tests.
stages.prove: A public GitHub with readable READMEs.

stages.title: HTTP, APIs and SQL
stages.goal: Serve data correctly and safely.
stages.build: A REST API for a real domain (library, clinic, shop) with Postgres, validation and auth.
stages.prove: An OpenAPI page and a Bruno collection committed to the repo.
stages.hint: Pick one framework in the language you chose. You do not need all of them.

stages.title: Ship it
stages.goal: Package, test and deploy like a team would.
stages.build: Dockerise the API, add CI that runs tests, add caching and deploy it.
stages.prove: A green CI badge and a live URL.

stages.title: Systems thinking
stages.goal: Reason about scale, failure and trade-offs.
stages.build: Rebuild a small piece of infrastructure (a Redis clone, a job queue) and write up the design.
stages.prove: A design doc and one CodeCrafters challenge completed.

name: Mobile app developer
summary: Build apps people install, from first screen to Play Store release.
outcome: Publish a polished app with offline data, notifications and analytics-free privacy.

stages.title: Pick a stack
stages.goal: Choose Flutter, native Android, iOS or React Native, and learn its language.
stages.build: Three single-screen apps: a counter, a form with validation and a list.
stages.prove: Screenshots and code on GitHub.
stages.hint: Pick one stack and stay with it until you ship an app.

stages.title: Real apps
stages.goal: Navigation, state and data from the network.
stages.build: A news or recipe app with navigation, a public API, caching and pull to refresh.
stages.prove: A demo video in the README.

stages.title: Backend and storage
stages.goal: Accounts, a database and push notifications.
stages.build: Add sign-in, cloud data and notifications to your app.
stages.prove: A test account reviewers can use.

stages.title: Release
stages.goal: Make it reliable and ship it to a store.
stages.build: Publish on the Play Store or TestFlight with crash reporting and a privacy policy.
stages.prove: A store listing link on your resume.

name: Cloud and DevOps engineer
summary: Run software reliably on the cloud with Linux, containers, Kubernetes and IaC.
outcome: Provision infrastructure with code, deploy with pipelines and keep services observable.

stages.title: Linux and networking
stages.goal: Live in the terminal and understand how machines talk.
stages.build: A Linux server you set up yourself, hardened, with a website behind Nginx and HTTPS.
stages.prove: Bandit level 20 and notes on how you solved each level.

stages.title: One cloud, properly
stages.goal: Learn one provider deeply. AWS has the most jobs.
stages.build: The Cloud Resume Challenge, end to end.
stages.prove: AWS Solutions Architect Associate or AZ-104.
stages.hint: Pick one provider. AWS has the most job posts in India, Azure is common in service companies.

stages.title: Containers and CI/CD
stages.goal: Package everything and automate delivery.
stages.build: A pipeline that tests, builds an image and deploys an app on every push.
stages.prove: A public repo with the pipeline and a short write-up.

stages.title: Kubernetes and IaC
stages.goal: Run workloads at scale and describe infra as code.
stages.build: Terraform a cluster, deploy a three-service app with Helm, add monitoring and alerts.
stages.prove: CKA and Terraform Associate.

name: AI engineer
summary: Build useful products with machine learning and large language models.
outcome: Train, evaluate and ship ML and LLM features behind a real API, with evals.

stages.title: Python and maths you need
stages.goal: Python, NumPy, pandas and the intuition behind ML.
stages.build: Clean and explore two public datasets in notebooks with clear charts.
stages.prove: Notebooks published on Kaggle.

stages.title: Classic ML
stages.goal: Train, validate and explain models.
stages.build: One Kaggle Getting Started competition with a written approach.
stages.prove: A ranked submission and a public notebook.

stages.title: Deep learning and LLMs
stages.goal: How neural networks and transformers really work.
stages.build: Fine-tune a small open model on your own data and publish it.
stages.prove: A model or Space on your Hugging Face profile.

stages.title: AI engineering
stages.goal: RAG, tools, agents, evaluation and deployment.
stages.build: A RAG app over real documents with an eval set, served with FastAPI and deployed.
stages.prove: An eval report showing what you improved and how you measured it.
stages.hint: Start with one provider and one open model. The patterns transfer.

name: Data analyst
summary: Turn messy data into decisions with SQL, spreadsheets, Python and dashboards.
outcome: Answer business questions with SQL and Python and present them in a dashboard.

stages.title: Spreadsheets and SQL
stages.goal: The two skills every analyst job tests.
stages.build: Answer ten business questions on a public sales dataset using SQL only.
stages.prove: A GitHub repo with your queries and answers.

stages.title: Dashboards
stages.goal: Communicate numbers clearly.
stages.build: Two dashboards on public Indian data (for example data.gov.in), each answering one question.
stages.prove: Published dashboards and a one-page write-up each.

stages.title: Python for analysis
stages.goal: Clean, analyse and automate.
stages.build: An end-to-end analysis notebook from raw data to recommendations.
stages.prove: A Kaggle notebook and a short slide summary.

stages.title: Interview ready
stages.goal: Pass SQL and case rounds.
stages.build: Fifty SQL interview problems and two mock case studies.
stages.prove: PL-300 if you target Power BI roles.

name: Placements and DSA
role: Software engineer, campus and lateral hiring
summary: Crack online assessments and coding interviews with patterns, not memorising.
outcome: Solve medium problems in 30 minutes and explain your approach clearly.
start: One language you can code in

stages.title: Basics and one language
stages.goal: Arrays, strings, hashing, recursion and complexity.
stages.build: Solve 60 easy problems across topics in your interview language.
stages.prove: A streak on one platform and notes per pattern.

stages.title: Patterns
stages.goal: Two pointers, sliding window, stacks, trees, graphs and DP.
stages.build: Finish NeetCode 150 or Striver A2Z. Not both.
stages.prove: A pattern sheet in your own words.

stages.title: Speed
stages.goal: Contests and online assessment practice.
stages.build: One contest every week and upsolve after each.
stages.prove: A contest rating you can mention on your resume.

stages.title: Interviews
stages.goal: System design basics, projects and behavioural rounds.
stages.build: Mock interviews with friends: one coding, one design, one behavioural per week.
stages.prove: A one-page resume with numbers and live project links.

name: Cybersecurity
summary: Learn how systems are attacked so you can defend them.
outcome: Find, exploit and explain common vulnerabilities, and write clear reports.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.goal: Linux, networking and how the web works.
stages.build: Finish Bandit and TryHackMe Pre Security.
stages.prove: Write-ups on your own blog.

stages.title: Web security
stages.goal: The vulnerabilities behind most real breaches.
stages.build: All PortSwigger apprentice labs and a deliberately vulnerable app you secure.
stages.prove: A write-up for each lab category.

stages.title: Hands-on hacking
stages.goal: Real machines and capture the flag.
stages.build: Ten retired Hack The Box machines with full reports.
stages.prove: Security+ for SOC and analyst roles.

stages.title: Specialise
stages.goal: Pick SOC, pentesting, AppSec or cloud security.
stages.build: Play a CTF with a team every month and report one real bug on a bounty programme.
stages.prove: OSCP only if pentesting is your goal.
